title: Compact tenant + route pattern signatures for fast SLA & cost slicing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: per-route and per-tenant SLA/cost queries currently scan wide invocation fact tables with dozens of join keys. High-cardinality attributes (route patterns, feature flags, model_variant) blow out storage and slow ad-hoc SLO slicing. Goal: build a compact, query-friendly mart of 'invocation signatures' — small hashed signatures capturing the essential dimension set for fast approximate grouping and incremental joins for accurate attribution when needed.
acceptance_criteria: New signature mart (weekly partitions) populated for last 90 days and incrementally maintained
Common SLO queries (p50/p95 latency by tenant x route pattern x model_variant) execute <= 5s on 1T raw invocations using signature-first joins
End-to-end cost attribution accuracy within 1% of canonical full-join pipeline for top-90% traffic tenants (sampled verification)
Backfill and cutover plan executed with no consumer disruptions; legacy queries redirected by feature flag
technical_notes: Schema: (week_partition, tenant_id, signature_hash, hll_route_patterns, sample_invocation_ids, aggregate_tokens, agg_latency_p50, agg_latency_p95, invocation_count)

Signature generation: stable murmur3 hash of normalized route pattern + model_variant + feature_flag_bitmap + invocation_bucket (temporal 1-minute bin). Keep full route_pattern->signature mapping for high-fidelity joins with lower frequency.

Compression: store HLL sketches (12-byte registers) for cardinalities, and LZ4-compressed arrays for sampled invocation ids. Write Parquet with dict-encoded signature_hash and snappy row-group sizing tuned for ~200MB files.
Partitioning: weekly partition + tenant_id bucket (mod 64) to limit small-file explosion for large tenants. Consider daily for super-high-volume tenants; will add dynamic partitioning later.

Approx algos: HLL for distinct route patterns, t-digest for approximate latency percentiles where sample-based aggregation is sufficient. Full percentile fallback uses sampled invocation_ids join to canonical invocation table (on demand).

Query flow: user query hits signature mart to identify top-K signatures for tenant/time-range. Then a narrower join to canonical invocations table for exact aggregates if requested. This reduces scan size by 10-100x in practice.
Compatibility: expose a view console.signature_route_mart that contains decoded route_hint and sample pointers to enable existing dashboards to switch over with minimal refactor.
Storage estimate: ~2-4GB per week for global albeit skewed; aim for 90-day retention in primary hot store and archive older partitions to cheaper storage tier with reprovision option.
Data freshness SLA: initial goal T+15m for nearline pipeline; can change to T+5m for high-priority tenants in Dedicated later.
migration_plan: Phase 0 (design): finalize signature fields and hash seed. Done. Spec: docs.google.com/document/d/1abc-signature-mart-spec
Phase 1 (pilot): generate signatures for 7-day window for 5 high-volume tenants. Run validation queries comparing full-join outputs. (Owner: Marco) - in progress
Phase 2 (backfill): run distributed backfill for 90 days; monitor DQ checks. Use job ID: gh-PR-4822 to coordinate compute resources.
Phase 3 (cutover): create feature-flagged view console.signature_route_mart_v1 and flip dashboards one-by-one. Maintain fallback to canonical joins for 30 days.
Phase 4 (optimize): add tenant-specific daily partitions and fine-tune Parquet row-group size based on observed read patterns.
queries_examples:
-- find top signatures for tenant in window
SELECT signature_hash, invocation_count, hll_cardinality(hll_route_patterns) as route_card FROM console.signature_route_mart WHERE tenant_id = 't_123' AND week_partition = '2025-02-09' ORDER BY invocation_count DESC LIMIT 50;

-- approximate SLO slice using mart only
SELECT tenant_id, signature_hash, invocation_count, agg_latency_p95 FROM console.signature_route_mart WHERE tenant_id = 't_123' AND signature_hash IN (<top-k>);

-- exact rollup for small subset using sample_invocation_ids
SELECT AVG(latency) FROM invocation_canonical WHERE invocation_id IN (SELECT unnest(sample_invocation_ids) FROM console.signature_route_mart WHERE signature_hash = '0x9f7a');
metrics_and_dashboards: mart_ingest_latency_ms: histogram of pipeline latency per partition
mart_population_coverage_pct: percentage of total invocations covered by signatures per tenant
dq_mismatch_rate: percent difference between mart-derived aggregates and canonical pipeline (sampled)
console:signature-mart uptake dashboard for dashboards migrated vs. fallback counts
comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha: Initial spec posted. Asked data-privacy team if storing sampled invocation_ids is acceptable. Pending review.
2025-02-18 - Marco: Pilot job queued for 3 high-volume tenants. Using mu-spark cluster; estimate 6h runtime for 7-day window.
2025-02-22 - Priya (Data Privacy): Approved storing hashed signatures and sampled ids with 30-day retention. Must redact user-sensitive metadata prior to sample export.
2025-02-27 - Eng-Pair Review: Decided to use murmur3 seed 0xA5A5 for cross-system stability; avoid salted hashes per tenant to keep joinability.
2025-03-01 - Marco: Pilot completed. Coverage 92% for pilot tenants; dq_mismatch_rate 0.6% against canonical. Scheduling full 90-day backfill next week (job gh-PR-4890).
